1️⃣ Repository Identity & Discoverability
Create the GitHub repository and push a baseline commit
DESCRIPTION: Create or connect the repository, set main as the default branch, and push a baseline commit (for example README and LICENSE) so issues, automation, and collaboration all target a stable branch from day one.

CONTENT: Create and commit a project-appropriate .gitignore
DESCRIPTION: Add a .gitignore tailored to the tech stack before committing application code so build outputs, secrets, and machine-specific files are not tracked.

CONTENT: Verify the owner or organisation profile image is up to date and clear at small sizes @people-self @place-anywhere @tools-github @when-anytime @duration-10m
DESCRIPTION: If this repository is public or intended to be discoverable, check that the visible GitHub account or organisation profile image is current, easy to recognise at small sizes, and consistent with the project or brand. Prefer a simple image with clear contrast so people can identify the repository source in search results, notifications, and activity feeds.

CONTENT: Name the repository in kebab-case with clear purpose and audience keywords @people-self @place-anywhere @tools-github @when-anytime @duration-10m
DESCRIPTION: Choose a concise repository name using lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens only. Include terms that state the project purpose and primary audience so the name is easy to scan in GitHub lists and easier to find via keyword search. Check availability on GitHub before committing - renaming later breaks clone URLs, published links, and dependent automation. Avoid vague or internal-only wording unless it is a recognised team standard. If the repository will be published as a package or hosted on GitHub Pages, verify the name also works as a valid package name or subdomain path.

CONTENT: Write a concise repository description with purpose, audience, and keywords
DESCRIPTION: Write a single sentence that explains what the repository does, who it helps, and the main value it provides. Use plain language and include one or two words people are likely to search for so it is easier to find in GitHub search and quicker to understand in lists and profile views.

CONTENT: Add relevant and descriptive repository topics to improve search discoverability
DESCRIPTION: Review the repository purpose and add 5 to 10 specific GitHub topics covering language, framework, domain, and use case so the project is easier to find in topic search.

CONTENT: Decide and set repository visibility before the first push (Public or Private) @people-self @place-anywhere @tools-github @when-anytime @duration-10m
DESCRIPTION: Choose whether the repository should be Public or Private before the first push, based on discoverability, collaboration, and compliance needs. Document the decision in the README or setup notes and verify it matches your organisation policy and access expectations.

CONTENT: Pin this repo to your GitHub profile if it is active or strategically important @people-self @place-anywhere @tools-github @when-anytime @duration-10m
DESCRIPTION: Review your pinned repositories and pin this repo only if it is active, strategically important, or a high-priority project you want visitors to notice first. Keep the list curated by removing stale or lower-priority pins so your profile reflects your current focus.

CONTENT: Set the repository watch level intentionally (Not watching, Releases only, Watching, or Ignoring) @people-self @place-anywhere @tools-github @when-anytime @duration-10m
DESCRIPTION: Choose the lowest watch level that matches your role. Use Not watching to reduce noise, Releases only to follow releases without issue/PR noise, Watching for active maintainers, and Ignoring to mute notifications. Review after 2 weeks and adjust if you miss important updates or get too much noise.

CONTENT: Run the Repo Ecosystem Watch review and record Watch or Star decisions for related repos
DESCRIPTION: Review adjacent repositories in the same ecosystem and assign one action per repository. Use Watch for active projects you need to monitor and Star for useful references you may revisit. Record each repository and action in your notes so decisions are visible and repeatable.

CONTENT: Star this repository and add it to the best-fit GitHub list @people-self @place-anywhere @tools-github @when-anytime @duration-10m
DESCRIPTION: Choose one list with a clear purpose and audience so collaborators can find and scan it quickly.

CONTENT: Plan one GitHub automation workflow for repetitive repo work
DESCRIPTION: Find one repetitive repository task and define one automation workflow using GitHub Actions or GitHub Script. Include trigger, owner, expected outcome, and one success metric.

CONTENT: 2️⃣ Documentation & Knowledge Base
Write a user-focused problem statement in README.md (Markdown)
DESCRIPTION: Describe the problem this project solves, who experiences it, and the intended outcome in 3 to 6 plain-language bullet points. Keep markdown structure semantic (one clear H1, ordered H2/H3 headings, descriptive section titles) so screen-reader and search users can navigate quickly.

CONTENT: Document a concise architecture overview in README.md
DESCRIPTION: Describe the system context, core components, data flow, and key dependencies in a short architecture section. Add one simple diagram or step-by-step request-to-response flow, and organise content with a logical H2/H3 heading hierarchy and descriptive section titles so readers can quickly scan behaviour and integration points. If you include an image diagram, provide specific alt text that summarises the architecture.

CONTENT: Add representative screenshots or diagrams to README.md
DESCRIPTION: Add 1 to 3 visuals that help a first-time visitor understand the product, workflow, or output within seconds. Prefer annotated screenshots for user-facing flows and simple architecture or process diagrams for systems work. Place each visual near the relevant section, use concise captions, and write alt text that explains the purpose and key information shown rather than the file name. Optimise image size for fast loading, keep styling consistent, and verify the visuals still make sense in dark mode, on mobile, and when images fail to load.

CONTENT: Add clear local setup and run guide to README.md
DESCRIPTION: Document prerequisites, install steps, environment/config setup, and first-run commands in order. Include one expected success check (for example command output or URL) and one troubleshooting step for a common setup failure.

CONTENT: Create and initialise CHANGELOG.md with an Unreleased section
DESCRIPTION: Use a Keep a Changelog-style format with an Unreleased section, clear version headings, and dated entries so future changes can be tracked consistently from the first release.

CONTENT: Create or update a Roadmap section in README.md with short- and medium-term milestones.
DESCRIPTION: Add outcome-based milestones for the next 3-6 months, using clear status labels (Planned, In Progress, Done) and owner names where relevant; keep entries concise and scannable as bullets.

CONTENT: Enable the project wiki and add a Problem Statement page
DESCRIPTION: Enable the wiki, then create a dedicated Problem Statement page that expands the README statement with project context, key constraints, and links to related decisions.

CONTENT: Create a technical architecture wiki page with system boundaries and interfaces
DESCRIPTION: Document system boundaries, core modules, key interfaces, integration points, and non-functional requirements. Include one current architecture diagram, add links to related decisions, and keep terminology aligned with README.md to reduce documentation drift.

CONTENT: Create a wiki screenshots page with workflow-grouped visuals
DESCRIPTION: Create a dedicated screenshots page grouped by workflow so readers can quickly find relevant visuals. Use purpose-based alt text, concise captions, and last-updated notes; avoid placeholder or file-name alt text, and use empty alt text only for decorative images so visual documentation remains accessible and maintainable.

CONTENT: Add a setup guide page to the wiki
DESCRIPTION: Provide step-by-step local setup and environment guidance with command examples and verification checks. Link back to README quick-start for discoverability.

CONTENT: Add a roadmap page to the wiki
DESCRIPTION: Mirror the roadmap intent from README and expand each milestone with scope, dependencies, and success criteria. Review monthly to keep it current.

CONTENT: Configure GitHub Pages for docs or a project site (if applicable)
DESCRIPTION: Choose source branch/folder, set a custom domain if used, and verify published pages load correctly with working navigation and metadata.

CONTENT: Add and deploy a valid robots.txt for the GitHub Pages site
DESCRIPTION: Ensure /robots.txt is publicly accessible after deploy and contains valid directives, including User-agent: * and intentional Allow/Disallow rules. Include an absolute Sitemap URL on the canonical production domain, verify indexable pages are not unintentionally blocked by robots meta tags or X-Robots-Tag headers, and run Lighthouse SEO to confirm no robots/indexing warnings remain.
